questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as used in Economics:

(i) Transfer Payment
(ii) Investment
(iii) Per Capita Income
(iv) Consumption
(v) Depreciation

(5 X 2 = 10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Transfer payment** is a payment made by the government (or another body) to individuals or groups for which no good or service is received in return, and which therefore does not come from current production. Examples: pensions, unemployment benefits, scholarships and subsidies. Transfer payments are not included in national income.

**(ii) Investment** is spending on *capital goods* (machines, factories, buildings, tools, roads) and on additions to stocks, with the aim of increasing the productive capacity of the economy in the future. It is not the buying of shares or land as such.

**(iii) Per capita income** is the national income of a country divided by its total population, that is, the average income per head.

$$
\text{Per capita income}=\frac{\text{National income}}{\text{Total population}}
$$

**(iv) Consumption** is the spending by households on goods and services to satisfy their present wants; it is also the using up of goods and services to satisfy wants.

**(v) Depreciation** (capital consumption) is the fall in the value of capital goods, such as machines and vehicles, over time because of wear and tear and obsolescence. It is deducted from gross national product to give net national product.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain Four (4) Factors that can increase the size of a country's National Income.

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** National income is the total value of goods and services produced by the residents of a country in a year (and the income earned from producing them). It can grow when more output is produced. The main factors are the following.

1. **Increase in the quantity of factors of production.** More labour (population growth, immigration, longer working hours), more land brought into use, and discovery of new natural resources such as oil or minerals increase the amount of output the country can produce, and so national income.
2. **Capital accumulation (higher investment).** When people save and firms and the government invest in machines, factories, roads, electricity and ports, each worker has more capital to work with, so output and national income rise. Foreign investment adds to this.
3. **Improvement in the quality of labour.** Education, training and better health care make workers more skilled and productive, so more is produced per worker.
4. **Technological progress.** New and better machines and methods of production (improved seeds, mechanised farming, computers) raise output from the same resources, increasing national income.
5. **Good government policies and political stability.** Peace, law and order, sound laws, fair taxes and incentives encourage savings, investment and business activity, which increase output.

(Any four, clearly explained, earn full marks.)

**Conclusion.** National income grows when the country has more and better factors of production, used with better technology in a stable environment.
